Our mission 

The YMCAs of Québec is a charitable organization 
that.contributes to the development of spirit, 
mind, and body, and to the well-being of 
individuals, families, and communities. 


Our Values 
Participation and access 
Education and prevention 
Respect for others 
Volunteer work and philanthropy 
Self-empowerment 


FROM THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC 


CONNECTED TO 


At The YMCAs of Québec, we are constantly striving to 
strengthen the communities we serve and to stay attuned 

to their needs. To this end, we have conducted a needs analysis 
of the communities served by each of our centres and we 
organized the very first YMCA Forum on the theme of 

“Building healthy communities.’ 


The YMCA has much to offer the community, and not just 
within our facilities. In addition to the ties being developed 
with the Secrétariat a la jeunesse, the Conférence Régionale 
des Elus (CRE) de Montréal, and Québec en forme, we have 
also established new partnerships with the borough of 
Outremont and the Centre jeunesse de Montréal, respectively 
for the management of an outdoor pool and a centre for 
supervised visitation. 


By surpassing the symbolic threshold of half a million dollars 
for the 2012 YMCA Strong Kids Campaign, by increasing our 
collaboration with other YMCAs across Canada, and through 
receiving your unwavering support for our efforts, we are 
better able to take effective action in building healthy 
communities for everyone, from young children to seniors. 


cjue Noe Allis 


Julie Mac Allister 
Chair of the Board of Directors 


Stéphane Vaillancourt 
President and CEO

FROM THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC FOUNDATION 


THE YMCAs OF QUEBEC FOUNDATION: 


Today's children and youth are faced with complex issues, 
and they do not all have the same opportunities to learn 
and grow strong. At the YMCA Foundation, we believe in 
equal opportunity: regardless of their family or financial 
situation, all children deserve the opportunity to reach their 
full potential. 


In 2012, we committed to increasing our fundraising efforts 
and conducted a strategic analysis of our activities. We 
adopted an action plan that emphasized the development 
of planned and major gifts, in order to involve individuals, 
foundations, and corporations who, like us, want to 
encourage children and youth from all walks of life to be 
more active, be successful at school, and develop their 
leadership skills. 


We would like to express special thanks to our colleagues 
from the Board of Directors and all our other donors to 
the Endowment Fund for always being mindful of the 
sustainability of our mission. This year, revenue from the 
Endowment Fund once again helped support several 
initiatives for children and youth. 


LGW 


Michael Goldbloom 
Chair of the Board of Directors 


I 


Laurent Giguére 
President of the Foundation 


Nuch uring the peténfial 
of 


Giving everyone equal opportunity to succeed: this was a 
common goal for several initiatives supported this year. Our 
Endowment Fund helped finance the creation of a music studio 
at Saint-Laurent and Notre-Dame-de-Grace, as well as our school 
retention (YMCA Alternative Suspension) and environmental 
engagement (C-Vert) programs in Québec; the Golf Tournament 
supported our Youth Zones; the YMCA Strong Kids Campaign 
allowed children—particularly those with special needs—to 
participate in our programs; and the Give With Target campaign 
benefitted our fitness programs for teens. 


The YMCA World Challenge, held on October 13, 2012, and 
organized by the World Alliance of YMCAs, aimed to introduce 
the YMCA as a global movement that fosters youth engagement 
by trying to shoot the greatest number of basketballs in one day. 
In Montréal, 1,678 people of all ages made over 5,000 throws and 
Canada ranked fifth out of 85 participating countries. Did we set 
a new Guinness World Record? Stay tuned... 


Over the last few years, YMCAs around the world have wanted 
their young leaders to have a greater say within the organization. 
This is why young people now participate in the governance of 
The YMCAs of Québec and its Board of Directors. We have also 
created a Youth Advisory Committee that is responsible for 
making recommendations to the Board of Directors with regard 
to strategies to implement within the community, particularly 
those that impact youth. A Young Leaders Forum has been 
created to allow employees and volunteers aged 18 to 30 to 
meet and discuss social issues that impact them. Let’s prepare 
tomorrow’s leaders!

THE YMCA TAKES TO THE GREAT OUTDOORS é 

What if, instead of offering physical activities in a traditional people Sayed ae eanonign 
setting, we brought the activities directly to you? Were you OUY GHATS Staten: 
aware that the YMCA offers free instructor-led physical activities 
in public spaces? In partnership with their respective boroughs, 
some of our YMCA centres offer Zumba, line-dancing, yoga, and 
Tai Chi classes outdoors in neighbouring parks. The YMCA has 
also created an outdoor intergenerational training circuit at 

the Cartierville YMCA. This type of initiative promotes an active 
lifestyle for neighbourhood residents in particular.

It is a little known fact that Montréal is a 
hub for human trafficking. Modern-day 
slavery can take many forms: child soldiers, 
prostitution, and forced agricultural or 
domestic workers. Stop Child Trafficking 
is an awareness-raising project developed 
by The YMCAs of Québec’s International 
Initiatives and financed by the Ministére 
des Relations internationales du Québec’s 
Public Fund for International Solidarity 
Education and Participation. Let’s stand

PROVIDING YOUTH WITH THE 
TOOLS TO BECOME AGENTS 

OF CHANGE 

At the International Youth Engagement 
Summit, financed through funds raised by 
the Peace Medals, 50 youths interested in 
making a difference—10 of whom were 
representatives from our international 
partners—came together to re-invent 
the world during four days filled with 
workshops and discussions at YMCA 
Camp Kanawana. Held between 

August 30 and September 3, 2012, 

the aim of the summit—on the theme 

of “From well-being to community 
engagement!”, was to develop leadership 
skills and citizen engagement among 


youth aged 16 to 25 from here and abroad. 


It was the first of many summits to be 
organized by and for youth.

of Québec.

MEETING THE NEEDS OF THE COMMUNITY 
In order to continue making a positive impact on people's lives, 


we conducted a needs analysis of the communities around 

our centres, surveying more than 200 influential people from the 

community. Two main issues emerged: the health of youth and O5 people anaes in our community 
support for seniors, both in terms of the growing needs of these mn development and international solidarity 
two populations, as well as the leading role the YMCA could and programs 

should play in both areas. The next step: work together across the ; 

association and prepare five-year action plans by centre. 

BUILDING A PHYSICALLY ACTIVE COMMUNITY 

On December 5, The YMCAs of Québec presented a brief to people saw their quality of life 

the city of Montréal’s Commission sur la culture, le patrimoine improved through our recreation 


et les sports as part of Montréal, physically active, a public programs. 
consultation on how to get Montréalers more active. True to 
our mission, we shared our vision for an active city focused on 
the values of accessibility, inclusion, and adaptability. We believe 
we can increase Montréalers’ participation in physical activities 
and eliminate access inequality by encouraging volunteerism 
and building partnerships. 


FOSTERING LOCAL DEVELOPMENT AND 
INTERNATIONAL SOLIDARITY 

Last May, as part of a support program born of a collaboration 
between The YMCAs of Québec, UNI-Alter, and Alternatives, over 
70 people—delegates from Québec civil society—participated 
in the People’s Summit for Social and Environmental Justice 

in defence of the commons in Brazil. This summit was held 

in concert with Rio+20, the United Nations Conference on 
Sustainable Development. Five young Aboriginal women 

were selected to share their vision of sustainable development 
with Aboriginal women from Brazil.

Referred to the Institut Nazareth et 
Louis-Braille and Institut Raymond-Dewar 
(INLB-IRD) and encouraged by her son, 
68-year-old Diane Thériault, who is 
visually and hearing impaired, visits the 
Hochelaga-Maisonneuve YMCA twice a 
week as part of the YMCA‘s Integrated 
Recreation program. She does so in the 
company of her dog, Patch. 


There, she receives the support of 

her volunteer, Sandra Aziz, age 21, 

a third-year psychology major who 
helps her safely participate in physical 
activities: “Exercising has given me 
confidence and helped me get back in 
shape.” Without Sandra, Diane would 
simply not have access to fitness 
training. 


Mel 


Both enjoy their experience and they 
get along famously. Sandra confirms it: 
“|get as much out of it as | give!”

Sandra‘s testimonials.

EXTENDED OUTREACH 

The YMCAs of Québec collaborates 

with various schools and school boards 
throughout the province to deliver 
programs such as YMCA Youth Exchanges 
Canada and Summer Work Student 
Exchange in communities across Québec, 
from Rouyn-Noranda to Riviére-Saint-Paul, 
and as far as Kawawachikamak. 


In collaboration with many partners, 

The YMCAs of Québec also operates 16 other 
service sites across Canada through the 
YMCA Alternative Suspension program.
